name: Saint Gregory Barbarigo
history: A Venetian nobleman and diplomat who became a priest, cardinal and model bishop of the reform of Trent, first at Bergamo and then for over thirty years at Padua. He nursed the sick in the Roman plague, visited every parish, founded a great seminary with its own press, and longed for reunion with the Christians of the East.
life: Gregorio Barbarigo, of an old Venetian family, accompanied the Venetian ambassador to the peace talks at Münster that ended the Thirty Years’ War, and there met the papal envoy, the future Alexander VII, who encouraged his vocation. Ordained in 1655, he worked in Rome during the plague of 1656, caring for the sick and dying. He was made bishop of Bergamo in 1657 and cardinal in 1660, and in 1664 was moved to Padua, where he stayed until his death. Taking Saint Charles Borromeo as his model, he visited every parish, taught catechism himself, and gave away so much that he was often short of money. His seminary at Padua became famous for learning, and its press printed books in Greek, Arabic and other languages of the East, in hope of unity with separated Christians. John XXIII, who had served at Bergamo, canonised him in 1960.
prayerTo: Saint Gregory, faithful shepherd, you served the plague-stricken, taught the children and spent yourself for your people. Pray for our bishops and priests, for seminarians, and for the unity of Christians of East and West. Help me to serve gladly, without counting the cost. Amen.
penance: Pray today for your bishop and for your diocesan seminarians by name if you know them, and give something to support their formation.
meditation: He carried the plans of a reformer and the purse of a poor man. What would change in your parish if you gave it a little more of your time?
prayer: O God, Who have willed that Blessed Gregory, Your Confessor and Bishop, be renowned for the care of his flock and compassion for the poor; favorably grant that we who honor his merits may imitate the example of his charity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
